extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and research administrators preparing applications to Royal Society funding schemes (UK and international), and host UK universities / not-for-profit research institutions
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance and principles for applying to Royal Society grants and fellowships (e.g., Wolfson Fellowship), describing what the Society funds, who should apply, and procedural requirements such as deadlines, policies and the assessment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding aims: freedom, support and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society funding provides freedom, support and flexibility to researchers in the UK and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the high-level expectation that awards are intended to give researchers autonomy and practical support; implies applications should explain how funding will enable researcher freedom and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal Society Wolfson Fellowship — institutional eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The five-year Royal Society Wolfson Fellowships enables UK universities and not-for-profit research institutions to attract and recruit talented…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates scheme is aimed at UK universities and not-for-profit research institutions to recruit talent; page also lists a closing date (Closing 01 July 2026) — applicants must note scheme-specific eligibility and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for discovery-led and applied research
rubrics_metrics.description: We support scientists pursuing discovery-led and applied research through a wide range of schemes and career development opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate how their work is discovery-led and/or applied and how it aligns with available schemes and development opportunities offered by the Society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity is essential; encourage broad applicant backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for delivering excellence in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences to maximise innovation and creativity in science for the benefit of humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation that applications and host institutions support diversity and inclusion; applicants from diverse backgrounds are explicitly encouraged and selection will be informed by diversity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles: Excellence; Inclusivity; Flexibility; and Openness and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is guided by the principles of Excellence; Inclusivity; Flexibility; and Openness and Fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four principles frame how the Society evaluates and administers funding — applications should reflect excellence in research, inclusive practices, flexible approaches where appropriate, and openness/fairness in conduct and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the application and assessment process
rubrics_metrics.description: A step-by-step guide to the application and assessment process for our schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to follow the Society's specified application steps and the stated assessment process; deviations may affect eligibility or assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to key dates (open, close, decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: See key dates for funding schemes, with open, close and decision dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and decision dates are mandatory scheduling constraints for applications — timely submission is required and relevant to eligibility/consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take up training and development opportunities as a grant-holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Find out about the tailored career development and engagement opportunities available to many of our grant-holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees are expected or encouraged to participate in Society-provided career development and engagement activities; applicants may reference intended engagement with these opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with policies and positions underpinning the grants portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: View the policies and positions underpinning our grants portfolio – relevant to all applicants and award holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and award-holders must follow the Society's policies (e.g., eligibility, research integrity, data/ethical policies); non-compliance may affect award or administration.
